headline: Oil retreat and earnings beats lift the Dow 1% and small caps 1.8%; Nasdaq flat as AI lags
summary: A broad rotation day. Stocks opened lower as AI shares slid after a 3.7% drop in Korea's Kospi and Brent neared $112, then turned up within the first hour as oil reversed and the Dow added about 600 points by mid-morning. More than 400 S&P 500 stocks rose and eight of 11 sectors gained, led by record-high healthcare, while technology, communication services and energy fell and late selling left the Nasdaq a hair lower.
drivers: Oil reverses from a five-month high

Brent hit nearly $112 on Gulf shipping attacks and Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, then fell 0.7% to $108.79 on signs of continuing US-Iran talks and eased Russia sanctions; December WTI settled 0.7% lower at $97.82. Airlines rallied (American +3.7%, United +2.3%) and the 10-year yield slipped about 3bp to 5.11%.

3M rose 5.8% after beating and raising its outlook, Equifax jumped 11.3%, Hasbro 11.2% and Northrop Grumman more than 4%. GM fell 6.8% despite a beat and a $20B buyback, as its full-year profit range disappointed on about $2B of raw-material costs.

Healthcare rose about 2.4% to a record, with Eli Lilly up about 4% as the biggest boost to the S&P 500 and gains in UnitedHealth, Merck, J&J and Amgen. Real estate (+1.7%), utilities and financials (+1.2% each) also gained; Braze soared 52% on a $47.50-a-share Salesforce bid.
AI and Big Tech still lag

Chips sank to their lowest since early August at the open before bargain buyers cut the losses, but equipment makers (Lam, KLA, Applied) stayed weak and tech ended down 0.3%. Meta fell about 2% and Apple and Alphabet also slipped; CoreWeave swung from −6% to +5% and closed up 1.7% while its default-swap spread topped 1,100bp.
week: Week so far: Russell 2000 +1.9%, Nasdaq +1.1%, Dow +0.9%, S&P 500 +0.7%, as leadership shifts from Monday's tech bounce to the broader market. November WTI expired Tuesday at $101.79 (−1.8%), so the oil row now tracks December; the 10-year yield remains above 5% with Brent stuck in a $97–112 range this month.
watch: Next: SpaceX beat forecasts after the close with revenue up 161% while Netflix fell after hours; Meta and Tesla report Wednesday and Lam Research this week, with the Fed meeting next week.
